title: Sync task planning between hosts with one operator command on the folder route
outcome: Sync task planning between hosts with one operator command on the folder route
acceptance: One operator command on the folder route (scripts/task-sync-folder.mjs) exports this host's planning, fetches the data branch, three-way merges task files against the last imported or published commit, imports with a dry run first, commits a fast-forward and pushes the data branch, using only shipped engram commands and plain Git (no force, rebase, pull or merge commit)

It stops visibly with a non-zero exit on any import refusal (printing the refusal code and per-task reasons verbatim), any text conflict (writing base, local and incoming versions), a task-file removal, or a repeated non-fast-forward rejection, and never depends on any particular refusal code
It runs on Windows and macOS

A behavior test drives two homes against a local bare remote: adds in both directions, concurrent edits of different tasks merged to a fast-forward, a same-field conflict stop, a non-fast-forward retry and an import refusal stop
docs/features/git-task-sync.md and docs/shipped.md describe the command
